shared_evidence.source: YouTube Help — Measure key moments for audience retention
shared_evidence.summary: YouTube exposes intro retention, top moments, spikes and dips and recommends using them to understand where viewers stay, rewatch or leave. Retention comparisons should account for similar-length videos; compelling later moments can be considered for earlier placement when story logic permits.

shared_evidence.source: YouTube Help — impressions/CTR and recommendation guidance
shared_evidence.summary: Packaging and early content should fulfill the title/thumbnail promise. CTR should not be optimized without watch/retention guardrails; misleading clickbait is not a durable strategy.

shared_evidence.source: LangGraph official docs — durable execution and persistence
shared_evidence.summary: Durable execution depends on persistence/checkpointing and replay-safe workflow design. Side effects and non-deterministic operations should be isolated so interrupted workflows can resume without duplicating work.

Durable workflow systems persist execution state and resume after process or infrastructure failures. Activity retries, idempotency and explicit workflow state are key concepts; this is architecture evidence, not a mandate to adopt Temporal itself.

shared_evidence.source: AWS Builders Library — Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
shared_evidence.summary: Retries can amplify overload. Use timeouts, bounded retries, exponential backoff and jitter; make retried operations idempotent. Avoid retrying at multiple layers because multiplicative retry storms can result.

shared_evidence.source: Google Cloud retry guidance — exponential backoff
shared_evidence.summary: Transient failures should use bounded exponential backoff and only retry retryable conditions. Permanent errors require correction rather than repeated calls.

shared_evidence.source: GitHub Actions official docs — concurrency, dependency caching, artifacts, job timeout
shared_evidence.summary: Concurrency can prevent duplicate overlapping runs; caches are for reusable dependencies/accelerators while artifacts preserve outputs between jobs/runs. Jobs should have bounded timeouts. Workflow design should distinguish replaceable cache from durable evidence/output.

shared_evidence.source: FFmpeg official documentation — streamcopy, concat demuxer, segment muxer, ffprobe
shared_evidence.summary: Compatible scene outputs can be joined without unnecessary re-encoding using stream copy/concat. ffprobe provides machine-readable validation. Segmenting and scene-first production isolate failures but require media-contract compatibility.

shared_evidence.source: Adobe Premiere Pro official docs — Productions/proxy workflow
shared_evidence.summary: Long-form editing benefits from project/media organization and proxy workflows that reduce resource pressure while preserving high-quality source media for final output. This supports proxy/preflight as a selective accelerator, not a mandatory proxy for every scene.

Already requires scene-first rendering, content-addressed checkpoints, atomic scene promotion, ffprobe media contracts, bounded retries, process timeouts, preserved healthy outputs and cache/artifact role separation. It still has a stale 6-10 minute duration heuristic and older AI-division wording that should be checked against the user's 8-12 minute and compact ChatGPT+DeepSeek instructions.

A contradiction remains: older editing-profile fields require expression changes every 1-2 sentences and a hard fail after more than two sentences, while newer character-performance policy explicitly forbids fixed-interval expression changes. Newer semantic-beat policy should win and stale fixed-interval rules should be removed.

Future normal news/topic explainers target 8-12 minutes without padding via irrelevant history, repetition, slow narration or low-information filler. Runtime should be earned with relevant facts, mechanism, impact, material chronology, uncertainty and next watchpoints.
